chunks: And from him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

"Fasting of the month of Ramadan is by sighting (the moon), and not by conjecture. And indeed, the month of Ramadan may be twenty-nine days, and it may be thirty days, and it is subject to what other months are subject to, in terms of completion (thirty days) and deficiency (twenty-nine days)."
ai.seo_question: How is the start of Ramadan determined in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* underscores the Shia jurisprudential preference for actual visual sighting (ru'yah) over astronomical calculation (hisab) for initiating Ramadan, a stance that distinguishes it from other schools of thought. It further clarifies the natural variability of the lunar month, noting that Ramadan may be either twenty-nine or thirty days, mirroring the fluctuation of other lunar months. This ruling reinforces the importance of tangible evidence in religious observance, linking celestial phenomena directly to divine commandments.
